title: Differentiable Weightless Controllers: Learning Logic Circuits for Continuous Control
claim: Continuous inputs flow through binary encoding, layered lookup tables, summation and memory lookup to yield actions, using only logic operations.
layout: 1 panel, left-to-right, column headers labeling stages, dense wiring between table layers
description: A single black-and-white diagram reads left to right with bold column headers: Obs., Encoding, Lookup Tables, Memory, Acts. On the left, arrows enter observations obs_1 and obs_N, each feeding a short vertical stack of small squares (filled or hollow) that represent thermometer-encoded bits. Two columns of small 2x2 boolean lookup-table grids, filled with 0s and 1s, sit in the middle. Many thin black lines connect encoded bits to the first table layer and the first layer to the second in a sparse, crisscrossing pattern. The second layer's outputs go to circled plus nodes for group summation. Each sum feeds a rounded RAM box, then an arrow to act_0 or act_A. Vertical dots indicate omitted elements. The eye goes first to the tangled wiring in the center.
caption: Differentiable Weightless Controllers (DWCs): realvalued observations are thermometer-encoded into bitvectors, processed by two layers of multi-input boolean-output lookup tables (here drawn with 2 inputs), aggregated by group summation, and mapped via per-action memory lookups to final action values.
abstract: Controlling autonomous systems under real-world conditions often requires policies that can be evaluated with low latency and minimal energy consumption. Unfortunately, these conditions are at odds with the use of high-precision deep neural networks as controllers. In this work, we introduce Differentiable Weightless Controllers (DWCs), a symbolic-differentiable architecture that learns flexible, non-linear, yet highly efficient control policies. DWCs can be trained end-to-end via gradient-based techniques, yet compile directly into FPGA-compatible circuits with few- or even single-clock-cycle latency and nanojoule-level energy cost per action. Across five MuJoCo benchmarks, including high-dimensional Humanoid, DWCs achieve returns competitive with standard deep policies (full-precision or quantized neural networks). Furthermore, DWCs exhibit structurally sparse and interpretable connectivity patterns, enabling direct inspection of which input values influence control decisions.
